content:
So I've been working through Mathematics in Lean and am finding it increasingly straining on the eyes to read through proofs. This is the current syntax highlighting without having touched anything:

Am I doing something wrong? Is this the intended experience. I would love if lemmas, variables, compositions, show statements, cases, quantors and \l had different colors. It's already happening a little bit in the info view, where color, size and transparency are used to communicate information more clearly. Why not in the code itself?

Something like this I think could be nice

of course concrete colors for each token type are debatable but something akin to the info view would be nice
I think if you pick a different color scheme, local variables and constants receive different colors

Eric Wieser said:

I think if you pick a different color scheme, local variables and constants receive different colors

constants are blue atm which is nice, ive tried fiddling with vscode but it seems lean doesnt expose any token classifications other than variables, constants and keywords
Note that in your example, h really isn't any different to x y z

Eric Wieser said:

Note that in your example, h really isn't any different to x y z

okay. Why is that? I feel like proofs and variables should be treated differently, no?
Well, proofs are also variables. How would you color x' in have x' := x? Would it match x?
